passage: My name is Harish, and I remember the fractions test because my eyes kept sliding to the left. Bhavesh's page was right there, full of numbers. My pencil shook. I did not want another low mark, because last time Papa had gone quiet at dinner. Then something odd happened: I looked at the fear instead of the page. It was the fear that wanted me to peek, not me. I put my eyes back on my own paper and did what I could. Next morning I stayed after class and told Nirmala Ma'am, "I get scared in tests. Can you help me with fractions?" She smiled and gave me two evenings a week.

qa.q: What did Harish ask Nirmala Ma'am for?
qa.a: Harish asked for help with fractions.

qa.q: What did Harish realise about the urge to peek?
qa.a: That fear of another low mark was what made it tempting.

qa.q: What else could Harish do to ease test fear?
qa.a: Practise a few timed questions at home, because familiarity lowers the worry.

qa.q: How might Nirmala Ma'am see Harish's request?
qa.a: As an honest and brave step, since she smiled and offered two evenings a week.

grounding: A child afraid of low marks feels the pull to peek at a nearby page, names the fear, and asks the teacher for help instead.

Class teacher's note, Wednesday.
After today's maths test, Sumit stayed back. He told me something honest: during the test his eyes kept going to his neighbour's page. "I didn't copy, Ma'am. But I wanted to. I got scared I'd fail again, and then I wanted to look." He had worked it out himself: "It's not that I'm a cheater. It's that I'm scared. If I wasn't scared, I wouldn't want to look." Then he asked if I could give him extra practice in division, because that is where he feels lost. I told him I was glad he had told me. We have agreed on fifteen minutes after class on Tuesdays and Thursdays. I will also let his parents know that he asked for help himself.
Minakshi, class teacher

qa.q: When will the extra practice happen?
qa.a: Fifteen minutes after class on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

qa.q: What did Sumit realise about why he wanted to look?
qa.a: That fear of failing made cheating tempting; he felt scared, not dishonest.

qa.q: What else could help Sumit before the next test?
qa.a: Practising a few division sums at home each day, so he walks in less afraid.
Minakshi is glad he told her, sets up extra help, and plans to tell his parents he asked himself.

grounding: A teacher's note records a boy noticing that fear of low marks made peeking tempting, and asking for extra help instead.

Friday
Today in the English test I almost looked at Ayesha's paper. She sits so close, and I was stuck on the grammar part, and I kept thinking, what if I get a four again, what if Papa's face does that disappointed thing. My eyes started moving on their own. Then I stopped and thought: why do I want to look? Not because I'm bad. Because I'm scared. The scared feeling is doing the pulling. So I left that answer blank. After class I went to Mrs Rao and asked if she could help me with grammar before the next test. She said yes, Monday lunch. I feel lighter than I thought I would.
Varun

qa.q: What did Varun realise about the pull to look?
qa.a: That the scared feeling about a low mark was doing the pulling, not being a bad person.

qa.q: What else could Varun do before Monday?
qa.a: Varun could note which grammar questions were hardest, so the time with Mrs Rao goes further.

qa.q: How might Mrs Rao see Varun's request?
qa.a: Mrs Rao seems glad to help, agreeing straight away to Monday lunch.
